_comment: Every place the pipeline has to touch Google Flow's UI, in one file, because
Flow is a Radix SPA with hashed class names and it WILL move. When a run
fails with 'prompt box not found' or 'click target not found', this is the
file to edit — nothing else needs to change.
How to find a replacement: open the Flow project, right-click the control,
Inspect, and prefer in this order — a data- attribute, an aria-label, a
stable semantic tag. Never a hashed class name; those change on every Flow
deploy. `generate_text` matches on visible button text and is the most
durable of the three, which is why it is the default rather than a fallback.
`plate_input` is the file input behind Flow's reference-image control. It is
usually hidden and often only mounted once you have opened that panel, so if
set_image reports 'no file input matched', open the panel by hand once and
re-run — the pipeline is not able to click a control it cannot see.
`reference_clear` is the button that REMOVES an already-attached reference
image — the ✕ on the chip, or whatever Flow renders in its place. It is null
until somebody inspects the panel once and fills it in, and a null is
reported rather than worked around, because the failure it causes is silent:
emptying the file input does not clear the chips Flow has already rendered,
so one chained clip's carry frame rides along into the clip after next and
that clip is generated from two references, one of them stale. Everything
still runs; the sequence is just subtly wrong. `video veo` prints a warning
on every chained run until this is set.
`reference_panel` is the control that OPENS that panel, if Flow only mounts
the file input once it has been opened. Also optional: leave it null and open
the panel by hand once per session instead.
GENERATE, as found on the 2026-08 Flow build. The button is labelled
'Create', not 'Generate', and matching on that word is a TRAP: two visible
controls contain it — the submit arrow at the bottom right, and an
'Add media' dialog trigger at the bottom left. The text matcher prefers the
SHORTEST match, which is the dialog trigger, so a run would open a dialog,
submit nothing, and then wait fifteen minutes for a clip that was never
queued. That is why generate_selector is now set and takes precedence.
The selector says what the button IS: it reports its own enabled state
(aria-disabled) and is not a menu or dialog trigger (aria-haspopup). Both
Flow's hashed classes and the button's position are avoided. Verified
unique with the prompt box full AND empty.
generate_text is the fallback if that selector ever stops matching, and it
is 'arrow_forward' — the icon ligature, which appears in the submit
button's innerText and in no other control. Do NOT put 'create' there.
NOTE: this build reports aria-disabled='false' even when the prompt box is
EMPTY. So click()'s 'target is disabled -> the prompt did not land' guard
never fires here, and the real protection against submitting an empty box
is set_prompt's read-back check, which is verified and does work.
reference_open: the control on the PROMPT BAR that opens Flow's asset picker
(the add_2 button, aria-haspopup=dialog). null means the extension finds it by
heuristic, which works today. This is the control that ATTACHES an asset to the
next generation — distinct from plate_input, which only uploads into the project
library. Uploading without attaching is silent: the clip generates on an invented
background and the splice fails at both ends.
reference_chip_clear: the control that REMOVES one reference chip from the
prompt bar (usually an X revealed on hover). null lets the extension find it by
heuristic. Attaching is additive, so without clearing, references stack across
generations and Veo blends them — a stale chip from a hand test rode into the
first real run and it generated from two pictures with nothing in the log.
ATTACHING A BACKGROUND — the sequence, learned by watching it done by hand:
1. the + button on the prompt bar (add_2, aria-haspopup=dialog)
2. Upload media, in the panel that opens
3. pick the file
4. CLICK THE PHOTO — this is the step that attaches it; uploading alone does
nothing but add it to the project library.
What ATTACHED looks like, which is the reference the automation never had: a
50x50 element on the prompt bar holding one whose src carries the media
key, and whose own control reads "cancel" — the Material ligature for the X.
So the chip and its remove button are the same element. Counting any small
image near the prompt bar is NOT good enough: with the asset library panel open
that counted twelve chips on an empty prompt bar.
Also: the settings/mode control is now "tune - Settings", not the old
"Video - 720p - crop_9_16 - x1" chip. And Create reads aria-disabled=true while
the prompt box is empty, so in this state it is a usable pre-submit check.
THE PICKER IS SELECT-THEN-CONFIRM. It shows a list of assets on the left and a
preview on the right. Clicking a tile only moves the SELECTION; the asset is
attached by the "Add to Prompt" button under the preview. An older project
layout attached on the tile click alone, which is why skipping the confirm
appeared to work once and then never again. add_to_prompt now does both, and
verifies the chip carries the key it asked for — the picker attaches what is
selected, which is not always what was clicked.
